## The question

[Skull emoji 💀 in pdfLaTeX](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/761745/skull-emoji-in-pdflatex), asked by [Bryan](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/361821/bryan) on TeX Stack Exchange (2026-04-09; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I’d like to include the skull emoji 💀 in a document compiled with pdfLaTeX but with colors similar to how it displays on my device in other contexts.
>
> I can get a skull with `fontawesome`, but it’s not quite the same:
> ```latex
> \documentclass{scrartcl}
> \usepackage{fontawesome5}
> \begin{document}
> \faSkull
> \end{document}
> ```
> creates a skull like
>
> [![Skull emoji][q-1]][q-1] 
>
> which is black/white inverted compared to how my device normally shows 💀, where the skull is white, and the eye sockets are black.
>
> I cannot change to LuaTeX because what I am compiling is like, super large.
>
> I also tried something along the lines of ```\contourlength{0.5pt}``` and ```\contour{black}{\color{white}\faSkull}``` but that did not work well.
>
> Can anyone help get 💀 with black eye sockets on a white skull or something close to it? Thanks!
>
>   [q-1]: TMm0uygJ.png
:::

You could use LuaLaTeX and the [emoji][1] package.

```latex
% !TEX TS-program = lualatex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{emoji}
\begin{document}
\emoji{skull}
\end{document}
```

[![sample code output][3]][3]

From @jessexknight's comment, you can also use the [`twemojis`](https://www.ctan.org/pkg/twemojis) package in any LaTeX:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{twemojis}
\begin{document}
\twemoji{skull}
\end{document}
```

However, the image you get is [the one from the Twitter emojis library](https://emojipedia.org/twitter/twemoji-1.0/skull).

  [1]: https://ctan.org/pkg/emoji
  [3]: xF7COs2i.png
